stories.title: 1st Friday Focus on the Environment: Dingell talks environmental policy in a Democrat-controlled Congress
stories.summary: Congresswoman Debbie Dingell announced plans to introduce a 'Data Center Bill of Rights' to address environmental and infrastructure concerns surrounding large-scale data centers in her district. The proposed legislation aims to mandate transparency, independent monitoring, and community benefit agreements.

stories.title: Ann Arbor's iconic Blimpy Burger reopens under new ownership
stories.summary: Ann Arbor's Krazy Jim's Blimpy Burger has reopened following a seven-month closure under new local ownership. The establishment has introduced menu additions, including alcoholic beverages and soft-serve ice cream, while navigating community adjustments to operational changes ahead of a planned mid-November ribbon-cutting.

stories.title: El-Sayed claims victory, wins historic U.S. Senate race
stories.summary: Abdul El-Sayed, former Wayne County and Detroit health director, won Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat, becoming the nation's first Muslim U.S. senator. He defeated Republican Mike Rogers in a hard-fought race, campaigning on a progressive platform focused on healthcare, the environment, and economic issues.

inputFacts.title: Controversial Scarecrow Goes Missing
inputFacts.summary: A scarecrow depicting Dr. Frank-N-Furter from The Rocky Horror Picture Show, sponsored by PFLAG for Plymouth's annual Scarecrows in the Park event, was stolen from Kellogg Park on October 16. The display had previously sparked controversy and community debate regarding its appropriateness for a public park, though it also garnered significant support.

inputFacts.title: $250,000 investment from KeyBank Foundation to expand warming center and support for homeless adults
inputFacts.summary: A $250,000 investment from the KeyBank Foundation is expanding shelter and support services for homeless adults in Ypsilanti and eastern Washtenaw County. The funding supports a daytime resource hub and warming center at St. Luke’s Episcopal Church, providing case management, housing assistance, and basic necessities.

inputFacts.title: AADL celebrates books and authors with annual Printmaking Festival and A2 Community Bookfest
inputFacts.summary: The Ann Arbor District Library is hosting its annual Printmaking Festival and A2 Community Bookfest. These free events will include author talks, hands-on activities, and numerous vendors on November 14 and 15, 2026.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor Police Chief Anderson to retire
inputFacts.summary: Ann Arbor Police Chief Andre Anderson has announced his retirement, which will take effect in February. He previously addressed the City Council regarding a pilot program for an unarmed crisis response team.

inputFacts.title: Current Ann Arbor City Council holds its final meeting
inputFacts.summary: The Ann Arbor City Council held its final meeting of the current term. The session marked the last council meeting for Mayor Christopher Taylor.

inputFacts.title: Michigan Attorney General says no charges for deputies who shot Navy veteran
inputFacts.summary: The Michigan Attorney General's office has announced that no charges will be filed against Washtenaw County deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Navy veteran John Jenuwine. The incident occurred on January 6, 2026.

inputFacts.title: No. 5 Michigan women's basketball notches signature win over No. 2 UConn
inputFacts.summary: In her 15th season, coach Kim Barnes Arico led the Michigan women's basketball team to a significant victory against No. 2 UConn. This win marks a milestone for the program's development into a competitive power.

inputFacts.title: What Could Possibly Go Wrong? A Cabaret of Love, Lies, and Bad Decisions
inputFacts.summary: Theatre NOVA presents a musical fundraiser celebrating Broadway’s romantic mishaps and bad decisions from Nov. 6–15. The cabaret features local artists and supports the theater’s mission to produce original plays.

inputFacts.title: Where Steel Sharpens Steel: Inside Ypsilanti’s Decade-Long Hip-Hop Haven
inputFacts.summary: Visible prepares for a new creative milestone while The Dojo's founder Newcomb aims to secure financial stability for the independent arts space. The venue will host an event on Nov. 6 showcasing its role as a hip-hop incubator. After nearly a decade, the space continues fostering artist growth through performances and community connections.

inputFacts.title: Why are flags at half-staff today? Michigan honors late representative
inputFacts.summary: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer ordered U.S. and state flags to be flown at half-staff on November 5, 2026, to honor the late Jack Kirksey. Kirksey, a former state representative and mayor of Livonia, passed away on October 13 at the age of 97.

inputFacts.title: Washtenaw County voters came out in record numbers for 2026 midterms
inputFacts.summary: The Washtenaw County Clerk’s Office reported record voter turnout for the 2026 midterm elections, with over 202,000 ballots cast. County Clerk Larry Kestenbaum noted that the high volume of absentee and early voting influenced the outcomes of local measures, including the rejection of Proposal E.
